data.name: A Game of Thrones - Genesis
data.detailed_description:
What King will you be?
Conqueror, Usurper or Diplomat?
"A Game of Thrones - Genesis" immerses you into the heart of the battles and intrigues between the Houses that shaped the Kingdom of Westeros. From Nymeria's arrival in the Kingdom of Dorne to the awakening of the "Others" beyond the Wall, you'll live the origins of A Game of Thrones saga through more than 1000 years of history, by taking part in Westeros' founding events and largest battles.
In this great strategy game, victory does not necessarily result from brute force. You can choose to use a military approach and besiege your opponents, strangle them in an economical war, or even use dirty tricks and diplomacy to politically crush them. Treachery and deception are everywhere and can be more efficient than the most powerful army. So watch your back and show no mercy if you want to keep sat on the Iron Throne.

Key Features:

  • The video game adaptation of the fantasy saga "A Song of Ice and Fire" by George RR Martin.
  • A deep and exciting gameplay combining strategy, diplomacy and politics.
  • Discover the origins of the universe of the Iron Throne through the Story mode, and participate in major conflicts that have shaped Westeros.
  • Compete against up to 7 other players in multiplayer. Form alliances, break them, show subtle tactics and crush your opponents!

reviews.review:
This game is honestly pretty ambitious for what it is and in terms of a real attempt at the setting this RTS gets more hate than it deserves for trying to not be a generic RTS cash grab of a popular series.

The Good:
A series of campaigns set from 700 BC (10,000 Ships) to 300 AC (roughly until the middle of War of the Five Kings) so you get a sweeping portrait of Westeros through multiple periods. To be explicit it contains: 10,000 Ships (700BC ~ 680BC?), Aegon's Conquest (0BC - 4AC), Dance of Dragons (130AC), The Conquest of Dorne (157AC) [First] Blackfyre Rebellion (195 - 196AC), Robert's Rebellion (282AC), War of The Five Kings (299AC), The Wall (ie Wilding Migration South in the midst of WoTFK, 300AC)  

The Aegon's Conquest Campaign is awesome and lore accurate, its the second campaign after the Rhoynar one which is also good and are worth giving the game a try for alone

Unique Gameplay that melds tiers of units which you will have to manage and have a specific purpose. No super units (obv beside Dragons) and a meta that is rewarding,

Campaign does a good job of teaching you how to play the game, no tutorials here just good story + actually playing the game.

Multiplayer is a lot of fun if you have a friend

It has an Auto Save system that is pretty fair ingame and saves after every victory so you don't have to track saves  you can just play from where you left off 

Aegon's Dragon is awesome looking, the purple fire effect looks really cool when they burn castles.

Your Mileage May Vary

The AI plays an iterative game that is pretty predictable once you know how to play this game well (by the third campaign). The AI will seem good until you realize what its optimized for

The game is somehow not an HBO-licensed title so it doesn't even try to ape their aesthetic yet the designs stay true to a medieval fantasy setting. You will see some entirely unique visual takes on very familiar characters, locations, symbols, and units. I really liked Robert and Ned's portraits though that being said just be aware this is not HBO related and is far closer to the Novels in terms of their storytelling prose and structure. If you want something similar to the Game of Thrones RPG you will be shaken.

While the Rhoynar and Aegon's campaigns are of a respectable duration (about five levels with sub levels) every other succeeding campaign is abridged. This is most pronounced with the Dance of Dragons which really, if you're familiar with House of the Dragon, only shows the buildup to the fighting at Rook's Rest and some of the early Riverlands fighting before ending in an elaborate victory card explanation that, while accurate, would've been cool to play especially after Aegon's Conquest. 

You also really feel this jarring feeling with the Blackfyre Rebellion which is also a single level that tries to explain a bit too much. Personally I'm surprised they didn't try to do the War of the Ninepenny Kings before Robert's Rebellion to atleast show the start and end as well as transition into a recurring cast.

On this same note War of the Five Kings is pretty jarring to play as it opens in the aftermath of Mummer's Ford with Beric and Thoros (Brotherhood Without Banners) before skipping to Battle beneath the Wall a year later that is hamfisted together with a generic Night's Watch subplot (I guess they had to pad things out a little) and then just ending (so some of book 1, some of book 3, fin). It is really funny though how it says "oh btw if you wondered what happened to multiple protagonists since last mission, they died" lol

The game never got DLC, so what you see is what you get but when you play it long enough you may wish it had DLC or at least mods though there are plenty of GoT mods for other games ig 

Some of the smaller houses that should be a bigger deal aren't. The game has the following Houses available: Arryn, Tully, Stark, Baratheon, Tyrell (They double as Hightowers on some missions), Lannister, Targaryen, Dorne. This works for the historical campaigns or a historical themed versus match. However WoTFK has no Greyjoys (mentioned only), no Freys, no Boltons. This is no different for other periods which may get referenced but aren't ingame like: House Velaryon, Strong, Qorgyle which you will notice when playing and are a fan. 

No naval element or sea trade element, felt like a missed opportunity to not include sea trade and could've easily been a DLC for Greyjoys and Velaryon

As per no Naval Element the Iron Isles are often omitted from the game map in their actual form

While Essos is mentioned here and there it's otherwise not a factor ingame though I suppose a port mechanic would be needed. That also could've led to a Faith mechanic (similar to the game's Prestige mechanic that stops you from simply willing by killing everybody) and possibly some faith based agents but no thats not there...eh

The game has a strong "build up" meta where once you pass a tier of unit building (ie you can recruit Commanders and Army Units, not just Mercenaries or Guardsmen) the combat becomes very curb stomp like, especially if you're fighting against a player that owns the Red Keep and can recruit Dragons if so which can basically kill factions fast(often kills the faction lord leading to a passive loyalty loss for the faction, combined with miliary units you can sweep people quickly with it. Some people (like me) will find value in this due to the looooong midgame this game has, other's may find it a kind of lazy late game meta where your best path to winning based on how you played basically becomes obvious

There's not a big difference between the Houses. Another missed opportunity especially when the named hero units had neat skills.

The Bad:
The game is not well optimized for modern hardware yet there are patches online and modifications you can find online. It is kind of old school where it runs slower if you have other windows open and faster if its the only thing running while you play it

The game can be prone to crashing if you play multiple matches of it so be sure to reload your game when you finish campaigns and battles

The campaigns hold up pretty well until you get to WoTFK in which it seems like they just kind of ran out of time. Thoros gets an awesome portrait but then Beric gets THE MOST GENERIC KNIGHT PORTRAIT and The Wall just gave you some easy combat missions that say named characters are present but uses generic portraits for their characters. I most disliked how they did this for Jeor Mormont and Stannis who use generic Commander Models in the mission.

Definitely get it on sale if you are a GoT fan or an RTS fan who just wants to try something new. I really do hope we get a new game of this or a sequel some day because its foundation is very strong
